newsitem.title: USA: Owens Corning to buy Fibreboard for $515 million.
newsitem.headline: Owens Corning to buy Fibreboard for $515 million.

text.p: Building products company Owens Corning said Wednesday it would buy Fibreboard Corp. for $515 million in a deal that targets the growing vinyl siding industry.

Known mainly as a producer of insulation and roofing materials, the deal is expected to propel Owen Cornings' tiny two-year-old vinyl siding business into a major industry force. Fireboard is one of the nation's biggest producers of vinyl siding.
Under the plan, Owens Corning will buy Fireboard for $55 cash per share. The acquisition also calls for the assumption of $85 million in debt, bringing the total value to $600 million.

"Merging Fibreboard's businesses with Owens Corning will substantially strengthen our offering of building materials systems and make us a major producer and marketer of vinyl siding, one of the fastest growing products in the building materials market," Owens Corning Chairman Glen Hiner said.
The transaction is expected to quickly boost earnings for Owens Corning, generating an additional 5 cents per share this year and as much as 25 cents a share in 1998.
The company did not disclose a cost savings plan, but said it did not expect to close any of Fireboard's 21 manufacturing plants in the United States and Canada.
"We'll get some scale benefits, but mainly the big thing here is adding this product to our manufacturing base. This shows the market we're serious," said Owens spokesman William Hamilton.
Fibreboard, based in Walnut Creek, Calif., will become a wholly-owned subsidiary of Toledo, Ohio-based Owens Corning when the deal is completed in July.
Fibreboard Chief Operating Officer Ronald Mathewson will run the business, reporting to Jerry Weinstein, president of Owens' speciality and foam products division.
Fibreboard Chairman John Roach will serve as a consultant.

Hamilton said most of Owens Corning's efforts in the vinyl siding business have been aimed at the retail level. The acquisition of Fibreboard will give Owens Corning access to more than 130 distribution centres.

The planned transaction represents a change in strategy for Fibreboard, which had anticipated a series of acquisitions in its core building prodiucts business this year after selling its ski resorts division in late 1996. Earlier this month, it completed the $120 million purchase of closely held Fabwell Inc. in a transaction that was expected to increase Fibreboard's annual revenues by 40 percent.

News of the transaction sent Fibreboard stock soaring $6.75 to $54.25 on the American Stock Exchange, where it was the most heavily traded issue. Owens Corning added 50 cents to $41.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
The deal represents Owens Corning's 16th acquisition in the past three years and the largest to date.

Fibreboard, which also makes other residential and industrial building materials, had sales in 1996 of $469 million. Assuming its 1997 acquisitions had been completed on Jan. 1, Fibreboard's sales this year would approach an estimated $800 million.
Owens Corning had 1996 sales of $3.8 billion.
Under the agreement, Owens Corning will make a tender offer for all outstanding Fibreboard shares and certain options by June 3, subject to customary conditions.
Owens Corning said it would finance the transaction using a long-term bank credit facility underwritten by a major financial institution.
